## 8A. README, Documentation, and Changelog Discipline 📚

- Keep `README.md` a professional, approachable overview of the project's purpose, value, setup, usage, and links to deeper documentation. Keep it accurate as the project evolves.
- Put extensive technical explanations, architecture and design notes, implementation details, and long-form guides under `docs/` (or the repository's explicitly established documentation directory).
- Maintain chronological user-facing change history in the repository's established changelog, normally `CHANGELOG.md`, when a change history is used. Never turn the README into an accumulating changelog, internal progress log, or implementation-detail dump.
- Brief release highlights are appropriate in a README when genuinely helpful; keep the detailed history separate. Update documentation links and version references consistently when necessary.
limitations: Text-contract integrity is tested; no unobserved agent behavior is claimed.
Historical V0 and V1 artifacts are preserved and selectable.
